headline: Federer's comeback: the Australian Open at 35
text: Roger Federer beat Rafael Nadal in five sets in the Australian Open final, his 18th Grand Slam title and his first since 2012. He had missed half of 2016 after knee surgery. At 35 he is the oldest Grand Slam men's champion since 1972.
imageCaption: Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal in the Australian Open final, Melbourne, 29 January 2017
imageCredit: Phil Whitehouse from London, United Kingdom

headline: Citigroup returned $10.7 billion to shareholders in 2016
text: Citigroup reported fourth-quarter net income of $3.6 billion and said it returned $10.7 billion to shareholders in 2016 through dividends and share buybacks, buying back 196 million shares. In April 2016 it announced it would wind up Citi Holdings, its 'bad bank'.
imageCaption: Citicorp Center in New York

headline: The end of bank secrecy for foreign clients
text: From 2017 Switzerland applies the international standard for the automatic exchange of information on bank accounts: Swiss banks collect data on accounts of foreign residents, which will be sent to their home tax authorities from 2018. For depositors who do not live in Switzerland, bank secrecy is effectively over.
imageCaption: Credit Suisse's head office on Paradeplatz, Zurich

headline: Cisco buys AppDynamics on the eve of its IPO
text: Cisco agreed to buy AppDynamics, which monitors how business software performs, for $3.7 billion, a day before the start-up was to list its shares. Cisco is buying software companies to make up for slow growth in network hardware.
imageCaption: A building on Cisco's campus in San Jose

headline: Mark Schneider takes charge
text: Ulf Mark Schneider became chief executive of Nestlé in January, succeeding Paul Bulcke, who is to take over as chairman from Peter Brabeck-Letmathe.
imageCaption: Ulf Mark Schneider, the new chief executive of Nestlé

headline: The end of bank secrecy for foreign clients
text: From 2017 Switzerland applies the international standard for the automatic exchange of information on bank accounts: Swiss banks collect data on accounts of foreign residents, which will be sent to their home tax authorities from 2018. For depositors who do not live in Switzerland, bank secrecy is effectively over.
imageCaption: Paradeplatz in Zurich, the heart of Swiss banking

headline: McDonald's growth plan: digital, delivery and new restaurants
text: At an investor day on 1 March Steve Easterbrook presented McDonald's global growth plan: mobile ordering and other digital tools, home delivery, modernised 'Experience of the Future' restaurants in the US, new financial targets and a new three-year target for returning cash to shareholders.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000006390817000016/exhibit991.htm (release of 1 March 2017, read 2026-10-03); yearly change from data/out/mcd.json
imageCaption: Self-service ordering kiosks in a McDonald's, 2017 ;;

headline: Artificial intelligence triples Nvidia's data-centre sales
text: Nvidia's graphics chips were made for video games, but they turn out to be ideal for training artificial intelligence. On 9 May the company reported quarterly sales of 1.94 billion dollars, 48% more than a year earlier; sales to data centres almost tripled, from 143 to 409 million dollars. The shares rose 38% in May.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang (photograph from 2025)

headline: Amazon buys Whole Foods
text: Amazon agreed to buy Whole Foods Market, an upmarket supermarket chain with more than 400 stores, for about $13.7 billion. It is Amazon's first big step into physical shops.
imageCaption: A Whole Foods Market store, Ann Arbor, Michigan

headline: Immelt retires; John Flannery takes over
text: On 12 June General Electric announced that Jeff Immelt will retire and be replaced by John Flannery, head of its healthcare business. During Immelt's sixteen years, GE shares fell about 30% while the S&P 500 more than doubled.
imageCaption: John Flannery, named General Electric's next chief executive

headline: Activist Third Point buys in; Nestlé announces a $20.8 billion buyback
text: The American hedge fund Third Point of Daniel Loeb disclosed a stake worth about $3.5 billion in Nestlé and called for changes. Nestlé then announced a share buyback of about $20.8 billion.
imageCaption: Kit Kats in Japan (photograph from 2018)

headline: Federer's record eighth Wimbledon
text: Roger Federer beat Marin Čilić in the Wimbledon final without losing a set all tournament, his record eighth Wimbledon title and 19th Grand Slam title.
imageCaption: Roger Federer hits a forehand

headline: Cash floods in: Boeing raises its forecast
text: On 26 July Boeing reported strong second-quarter results, operating cash flow of 5 billion dollars and 2.5 billion dollars of share buybacks in the quarter, and raised its earnings and cash flow forecasts.
imageCaption: President Donald Trump and Boeing executives at the rollout of the 787-10, North Charleston, South Carolina, February 2017

headline: More coal: half of Hunter Valley Operations
text: After losing the contest for Rio Tinto's Coal & Allied to Yancoal, Glencore agreed on 27 July to buy 49% of the Hunter Valley Operations coal mine from Yancoal for $1.14bn in cash plus royalties. Coal and copper prices are rising: thermal coal averaged $88 a tonne in July and copper about $6,000.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/media-statement-49-in-hunter-valley-operations/4723797; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: An open-cut coal mine in the Hunter Valley, Australia

headline: Cartel allegations against German car makers
text: Reports in July said that German car makers, BMW among them, had coordinated technology, costs and suppliers in secret working groups for years, including on diesel exhaust cleaning. BMW denied colluding on emissions equipment.
source: The New York Times, 'BMW Denies Colluding With Carmakers on Emissions Equipment', 23 July 2017 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); Bloomberg, 'German Carmakers Can't Catch a Break as Next Scandal Looms Large', 21 July 2017 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The BMW tower and museum in Munich

headline: Diesel recall and cartel allegations
text: Daimler said on 18 July it will update the software of more than 3 million Mercedes diesel cars in Europe to cut emissions. Days later reports said German car makers including Daimler had for years coordinated technology in secret working groups, including on diesel exhaust cleaning.
source: The Guardian, 'Mercedes recalls 3m diesel cars over emissions concerns', 19 July 2017; Bloomberg, 'German Carmakers Can't Catch a Break as Next Scandal Looms Large', 21 July 2017 (headlines via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (2020 Clean Air Act fine, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Mercedes-Benz OM651 diesel engine, one of the engines in the recall

headline: Patent deal with Xiaomi
text: Nokia and the Chinese phone maker Xiaomi signed a business collaboration agreement and a multi-year patent cross-licence. Phones under the Nokia brand are back in shops this year, made by HMD Global under licence.
imageCaption: Lei Jun, Xiaomi's founder
imageCredit: Pool Moncloa/Borja Puig de la Bellacasa

headline: The first Model 3s are delivered
text: Tesla delivered the first Model 3s to customers in July. The cheaper car is meant to turn Tesla from a niche luxury maker into a mass producer. Tesla Motors renamed itself Tesla, Inc. in February.
imageCaption: The first production Tesla Model 3 outside the Fremont factory, July 2017

headline: The iPhone X
text: On 12 September Apple introduced the iPhone X, with facial recognition and wireless charging, alongside the iPhone 8, at the new Steve Jobs Theater.
imageCaption: The iPhone X with its box and accessories, November 2017

headline: Vas Narasimhan named next chief executive
text: Novartis named Vasant Narasimhan, its head of drug development and chief medical officer, to succeed Joseph Jimenez as chief executive in February. He is a 41-year-old American doctor who joined Novartis in 2005.
imageCaption: Vas Narasimhan, Novartis's chief executive

headline: GE halves its dividend
text: Under new chief executive John Flannery, General Electric cut its quarterly dividend in half, from 24 cents to 12 cents, its first cut since 2009. Earnings are heading for the low end of a reduced forecast, cash flow is weak, and the power business faces a shrinking market for gas turbines.
imageCaption: General Electric chief executive John Flannery presents his plan, including the halved dividend, to investors in New York, 13 November 2017

headline: A used rocket carries a used capsule to the space station
text: Rockets used to be thrown away after one flight. On 15 December SpaceX launched supplies for NASA from Cape Canaveral on a Falcon 9 rocket whose first stage had already flown in June, topped by a Dragon capsule that had been to space in 2015. It is the first time NASA has trusted a reused rocket. The first stage flew back and landed upright near the launch pad, and two days later the capsule reached the International Space Station with 2,205 kilograms of cargo.
imageCaption: SpaceX CRS-13, 2017

headline: 2017 in review: a calm climb and a big tax cut
text: The S&P 500 gained 19% in 2017 to 2,673.61 and the Dow 25.1%, after passing 20,000 on 25 January. On 22 December President Trump signed a tax law that cuts the corporate tax rate to a flat 21%. The Federal Reserve raised rates three times during the year.
imageCaption: American shares (S&P 500) at the end of each month of 2017: up 19 percent in the year
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC, month-end closes)

headline: Three rises in one year: the Fed's rate reaches 1.25 to 1.5 percent
text: The Fed raised its interest rate three times this year, on 15 March, 14 June and 13 December, each time by a quarter of a point, to a range of 1.25 to 1.5 percent. Nine years after the financial crisis the economy no longer needs free money, it says. By the standards of the past, borrowing is still very cheap. The numbers: the Fed's rate 1.3 percent. Inflation 2.2 percent. Unemployment 4.2 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to December 2017
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Disney agrees to buy most of 21st Century Fox
text: On 14 December Disney agreed to buy most of Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox, including its film studio and cable channels such as FX and National Geographic, for 52.4 billion dollars in Disney shares. Comcast had also bid.
imageCaption: Rupert Murdoch, 2009 ;;

headline: Sony sells its battery business
text: This year Sony sold its lithium-ion battery business, which it pioneered in 1991, to Murata Manufacturing, and closed its landmark Sony Building in Tokyo's Ginza for redevelopment. Sony's ADR rose about 60% during 2017.
imageCaption: The Sony Building in the Ginza district, Tokyo
